criterion_notes.c1: Examines community rural drinking-water supply via groundwater handpumps in Turkana County (northern Kenya) and The Gambia, specifically evaluating point-in-time water-point functionality, breakdown frequency, and downtime.
criterion_notes.c2: Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the study is a borderline exclude: although Table 2 lists institutional attributes (patent/design domain, supplier location, maintenance provider) and contextual interviews with maintenance service providers are invoked post-hoc in the Discussion to interpret repair-duration patterns (Diocese of Lodwar's subsidised flat annual repair tariff in Turkana; sole private supplier Swe-Gam vs local mechanics accommodating flexible payment in The Gambia; absence of formal national handpump standardisation policy), no legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor is empirically analysed as an identifiable exposure in the Results—handpump hardware model is the sole primary explanatory variable across all analyses, with maintenance provider unvaried in Turkana and completely collinear with pump brand in The Gambia. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, Criterion 2 is clearly not met: the evaluated exposure is physical water-lifting hardware technology (BluePump vs India Mark II, Afridev, and PB Mark II) alongside hydrogeological and physical covariates, while O&M service-delivery arrangements and standardisation remarks serve only as unanalysed contextual/project-delivery background rather than an empirically tested rule-type mechanism governing service access.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary empirical evidence from field inspections and community interviews at 142 handpump water points in Turkana and 161 in The Gambia (February–May 2016), analysed via univariable and multivariable logistic and linear regressions (n = 101 in Turkana; n = 89 in The Gambia), supplemented by Diocese of Lodwar repair records (2011–2015) and contextual stakeholder interviews.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports water-point service availability and reliability outcomes: point-in-time nonfunctional status (handpump did not produce water at inspection), >=1 breakdown in the previous 12 months, >=2 breakdowns in the previous 12 months, total annual downtime (days), and mean breakdown duration (days).
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies the unit of analysis and sample (community handpump water points in Turkana and The Gambia), the evaluated technological exposure (handpump model), the operational outcomes, and the cross-sectional comparative observational design.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is published in English.

evidence_quotes.quote: This study comparatively evaluated the operational performance of the BluePump against the Afridev, India Mark II and PB Mark II handpumps. The field assessment took place in Turkana County (northern Kenya) and The Gambia, contexts with contrasting environmental, social and institutional characteristics.

Handpump model formed the key explanatory variable of interest for all analyses. In Turkana, the BluePump was evaluated against the India Mark II and Afridev (no Duba handpumps met the eligibility criteria due to their relatively old age), while in The Gambia the India Mark II and PB Mark II were the comparison handpumps.
semistructured interviews were conducted with relevant implementing organisations and maintenance service providers, and a review of documents detailing maintenance activities was also carried out.
In total, 101 handpumps met the inclusion criteria in Turkana and 89 in The Gambia.
Relative to comparison handpumps, the BluePump had significantly lower odds of experiencing one or more breakdowns and two or more breakdowns in both Turkana and The Gambia

raw_response.exposure: Handpump water-lifting hardware technology/model (BluePump vs India Mark II and Afridev in Turkana; BluePump vs India Mark II and PB Mark II in The Gambia), controlling for static water level, handpump age, heavy usage, distance to urban centre, unconsolidated sediments, and twin handpumps
raw_response.outcome: Community water-point operational reliability and availability: point-in-time nonfunctionality at inspection, >=1 breakdown in previous 12 months, >=2 breakdowns in previous 12 months, total annual downtime (days), and average breakdown duration (days)
raw_response.population_and_sample: Community groundwater handpump water points (unit of analysis: water point / handpump); 142 visited in Turkana County, Kenya (101 meeting <=8-year age and non-dry/unsilted well criteria analysed in regressions) and 161 visited in The Gambia (89 analysed in regressions)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded as E03 (Wrong exposure). While the study empirically measures community drinking-water point functionality, breakdown frequency, and downtime in northern Kenya and The Gambia, its evaluated exposure across all analyses is handpump hardware technology (BluePump vs Afridev, India Mark II, and PB Mark II) and physical/hydrogeological covariates. Rural O&M service-delivery arrangements (Diocese of Lodwar's subsidised repair service in Turkana; private supplier Swe-Gam vs local mechanics in The Gambia) and national standardisation policies are discussed only qualitatively as unanalysed contextual background to interpret repair durations, rather than evaluated as a legal, administrative, or regulatory rule-type mechanism governing water access.
raw_response.study_design: Cross-sectional comparative observational field evaluation using water-point inspections, user interviews, and multivariable logistic and linear regression, contextualised by stakeholder interviews and maintenance records
